question: A group of ribosomes attached to mRNA is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is polysomes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A polysome (or polyribosome) is a cluster of ribosomes bound to a single strand of mRNA, simultaneously translating it to produce multiple copies of a protein. (पॉलिसोम — राइबोसोम समूह)

 

• Each ribosome in the cluster moves independently along the mRNA, synthesizing a complete polypeptide chain.

 

• Polysomes increase the efficiency of protein synthesis by allowing several polypeptides to be produced from a single mRNA transcript at the same time.

 

• Polysomes can occur freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming the rough ER.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A ribosome is made of two subunits (large and small), composed of rRNA and proteins, and is the site of translation (protein synthesis).

 

• The stage at which ribosomes attach to mRNA and begin translation is called initiation.

 

NOTE

 

• polypeptide (Option 1): This is the chain of amino acids that is the *product* of translation, not the ribosome-mRNA complex itself.

 

• polymer (Option 3): A general chemistry term for a large molecule made of repeating structural units; not specific to ribosome clusters.

 

• monomer (Option 4): A single repeating unit that combines to form a polymer; unrelated to ribosome-mRNA complexes.

question: Kelucharan Mohapatra, awarded with the Padma Vibhushan in the year 2000, was a dancer of which of the following classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926-2004) was a legendary guru of Odissi, credited with reviving and popularising it as a classical dance form. (केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिसी नृत्य)

 

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, in 2000.

 

• He earlier received the Padma Shri (1975) and Padma Bhushan (1988), and trained several eminent dancers including Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Madhavi Mudgal.

 

• He was also a skilled pakhawaj (percussion) player and painter, and served as a guru at the Kala Vikas Kendra, Cuttack.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha and is characterised by the tribhangi (three-bend) posture and fluid, sculpturesque movements.

 

• The Government of India instituted the "Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra National Award" in Odissi dance in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathakali (Option 2): A classical dance-drama of Kerala, known for elaborate makeup and costumes.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): A classical dance form of North India, associated with storytelling through rhythmic footwork.

 

• Manipuri (Option 4): A classical dance form of Manipur, known for its Raas Leela performances.

question: The Right to Freedom of Religion is contained within which Articles of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 25 to Article 28.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Freedom of Religion is one of the six Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Constitution, covered in Articles 25 to 28. (धर्म की स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 25-28)

 

• Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

 

• Article 26 guarantees freedom to manage religious affairs; Article 27 provides freedom from paying taxes for promotion of a particular religion; Article 28 provides freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions.

 

• These provisions collectively uphold India's secular character by guaranteeing religious freedom to all citizens, subject to public order, morality and health.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Right to Equality is covered under Articles 14-18; Right against Exploitation under Articles 23-24; Cultural and Educational Rights under Articles 29-30.

 

• Article 32, the Right to Constitutional Remedies, was called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 19 to Article 22 (Option 1): These cover the Right to Freedom (speech, assembly, movement, protection in respect of conviction, protection of life and personal liberty).

 

• Article 29 to Article 30 (Option 2): These cover Cultural and Educational Rights of minorities.

 

• Article 14 to Article 18 (Option 4): These cover the Right to Equality.

question: Which of the following is NOT an indirect tax?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wealth tax.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An indirect tax is one whose burden can be shifted to another person (usually levied on goods/services and passed to the consumer), whereas Wealth tax was a direct tax charged on a person's net wealth. (प्रत्यक्ष कर — वेल्थ टैक्स)

 

• Wealth tax in India was abolished in the Union Budget 2015-16 (effective AY 2016-17) and replaced with an additional surcharge on the super-rich.

 

• Excise tax, Customs duty, and GST are all indirect taxes, as their incidence can be passed on to the buyer of goods/services.

 

• Other direct taxes in India include Income Tax and Corporate Tax.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• GST was introduced in India on 1 July 2017, subsuming most existing indirect taxes such as VAT, service tax and excise duty.

 

• The CBIC (Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs) administers indirect taxes, while the CBDT (Central Board of Direct Taxes) administers direct taxes.

 

NOTE

 

• Excise tax (Option 1): An indirect tax levied on the manufacture of goods within the country.

 

• Goods and Services tax (Option 2): A comprehensive indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services.

 

• Customs duty (Option 3): An indirect tax levied on goods imported into (or exported from) the country.

question: Under which scheme, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha inaugurated "UMEED Market Place" in Jammu and Kashmir?
option_3: AVSAR Scheme of Airport Authority of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is AVSAR Scheme of Airport Authority of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In August 2022, J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha inaugurated "UMEED Market Place" at Srinagar Airport under the AVSAR (Airport Vendors Support for Atmanirbhar Rozgar) Scheme of the Airports Authority of India (AAI). (उम्मीद मार्केट प्लेस — एवसार योजना, AAI)

 

• The AVSAR scheme provides local artisans, weavers and self-help groups a platform at airports to sell indigenous, handmade products, promoting Atmanirbhar Bharat.

 

• UMEED Market Place showcases and sells products made by local artisans and Self Help Groups (SHGs) of Jammu & Kashmir to air travellers.

 

• The initiative supports the "Vocal for Local" vision by giving local products wider market access through airport retail space.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is a statutory body under the Ministry of Civil Aviation responsible for managing civil aviation infrastructure in India.

 

• Manoj Sinha has served as the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir since August 2020.

 

NOTE

 

• Stand Up India Scheme (Option 1): Launched in 2016 to promote entrepreneurship among women and SC/ST communities through bank loans; unrelated to airport retail.

 

• Ujjwala scheme (Option 2): The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides LPG connections to women from BPL households.

 

• KUSUM scheme (Option 4): The PM-KUSUM scheme promotes solar energy use among farmers.

question: The bird like pheasant and monals are found in which type of forest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Temperate deciduous forest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Birds like pheasants and monals inhabit the temperate deciduous forests found on the middle slopes of the Himalayas, roughly between 1,000 and 2,000 metres altitude. (शीतोष्ण पर्णपाती वन — तीतर और मोनाल)

 

• These forests occur in mid-latitude/mountain regions with distinct seasonal variation and are dominated by broad-leaved trees such as oak, chestnut, ash and maple that shed their leaves in a particular season.

 

• The diverse undergrowth and moderate climate of these temperate forests provide suitable habitat and food resources for pheasant and monal species.

 

• At higher altitudes, these deciduous forests give way to coniferous forests and, further up, to alpine grasslands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Himalayan Monal (*Lophophorus impejanus*) is the state bird of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, known for its iridescent multicoloured plumage.

 

• India's montane forests show a vertical zonation of vegetation, ranging from tropical at the foothills to alpine at the highest altitudes.

 

NOTE

 

• Tropical evergreen forest (Option 2): Found in high-rainfall areas like the Western Ghats and North-East India, hosting a different faunal assemblage.

 

• Temperate evergreen forest (Option 3): Found at higher altitudes with coniferous trees like pine, deodar and fir, above the deciduous zone.

 

• Mediterranean forests (Option 4): Found in regions with a Mediterranean-type climate, not a typical Himalayan habitat.

question: In which of the following years was the first train run in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1853.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853, between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane, covering about 34 km. (भारत की पहली रेलगाड़ी — 1853)

 

• The train was hauled by three steam locomotives named Sahib, Sindh and Sultan, carrying around 400 passengers in 14 carriages.

 

• This event marked the formal beginning of railway transport in India; 16 April is commemorated as a landmark date in Indian Railways' history.

 

• The Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR) operated this inaugural service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first railway budget was presented in 1924-25; Indian Railways today is among the largest railway networks in the world.

 

• Railway construction in India had begun a few years earlier, in the early 1850s, before the first train actually ran in 1853.

 

NOTE

 

• 1854 (Option 2): India's second railway line, from Howrah to Hooghly (~24 miles), opened this year under the East Indian Railway.

 

• 1852 (Option 3): Construction of the first railway line was underway around this time, but no train had run yet.

 

• 1855 (Option 4): Not associated with the first train run in India.

question: Which of the following dance forms is mentioned in the ancient text of Vyavaharmala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam, the classical dance form of Kerala, is mentioned in the ancient Malayalam text "Vyavaharamala", written by Mazhamangalam Narayanan Namboodiri in the 16th century. (मोहिनीअट्टम — व्यवहारमाला)

 

• Mohiniyattam derives its name from "Mohini", the enchantress female avatar of Lord Vishnu, and is performed solo by women with graceful, swaying movements.

 

• The dance form follows the Lasya style, emphasising gentle, feminine grace.

 

• It is accompanied by Carnatic music with Malayalam lyrics, and was revived and popularised in the 20th century largely due to poet Vallathol Narayana Menon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vallathol Narayana Menon founded the Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930, which played a key role in reviving Mohiniyattam and Kathakali.

 

• Kerala is also home to Kathakali and Koodiyattam (a Sanskrit theatre form recognised by UNESCO).

 

NOTE

 

• Sattriya (Option 1): The classical dance form of Assam, originating in the Sattras (Vaishnavite monasteries) of Srimanta Sankardeva.

 

• Manipuri (Option 3): The classical dance form of Manipur, associated with Vaishnavite Raas Leela themes.

 

• Odissi (Option 4): The classical dance form of Odisha, associated with temple traditions and the tribhangi posture.

question: The SI unit of electric charge is a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is coulomb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb (C), named after French physicist Charles-Augustin de Coulomb. (कूलॉम — विद्युत आवेश की इकाई)

 

• One coulomb is the amount of charge transported by a constant current of one ampere flowing for one second (1 C = 1 A × 1 s).

 

• Charge is a fundamental property of matter causing it to experience a force in an electromagnetic field; an electron carries a charge of approximately -1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

 

• Coulomb's Law, formulated by Charles-Augustin de Coulomb, describes the electrostatic force between two charged bodies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A), of resistance the ohm (Ω), and of electric potential the volt (V).

 

• Since 2019, the SI system defines the ampere by fixing the numerical value of the elementary charge; the coulomb is derived from it.

 

NOTE

 

• watt (Option 2): The SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second.

 

• newton (Option 3): The SI unit of force.

 

• joule (Option 4): The SI unit of energy or work.

question: In September 2022, the Supreme Court allowed all women, irrespective of their marital status, to safely and legally abort their child till ________of pregnancy under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24 weeks.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022 (X vs Principal Secretary, Health & Family Welfare Dept., NCT of Delhi), the Supreme Court ruled that all women, irrespective of marital status, have the right to safe and legal abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy under the MTP Act. (गर्भ समापन — 24 सप्ताह, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय 2022)

 

• The judgment extended the benefit of the amended MTP Act (2021) — earlier limiting unmarried women to 20 weeks — to bring parity between married and unmarried women.

 

• The Court also held that the definition of "rape" under the MTP Rules includes marital rape for the purpose of seeking abortion.

 

• The MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021 extended the general upper gestation limit from 20 to 24 weeks for certain categories of women (rape survivors, minors, women with foetal abnormalities, etc.).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original MTP Act was enacted in 1971 and amended in 2021 to expand access to safe abortion services in India.

 

• Beyond 24 weeks, termination requires the opinion of a Medical Board, mainly in cases of substantial foetal abnormalities.

 

NOTE

 

• 30 weeks (Option 1): Not the limit prescribed under the MTP Act as amended.

 

• 15 weeks (Option 2): Not the applicable threshold under the 2022 Supreme Court ruling.

 

• 18 weeks (Option 4): Not the applicable threshold under the 2022 Supreme Court ruling.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 120.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 120 of the Constitution deals with the language to be used in Parliament, stating that business shall be transacted in Hindi or English. (अनुच्छेद 120 — संसद की भाषा)

 

• It allows the presiding officer (Speaker/Chairman) to permit a member who cannot adequately express themselves in Hindi or English to address the House in their mother tongue.

 

• This provision falls under Part V of the Constitution (the Union), specifically the chapter on Parliament.

 

• English continued as an official language of Parliament beyond the originally envisaged 15-year transition period, under the Official Languages Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 343 declares Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union, with English continuing for official purposes.

 

• Article 348 deals with the language to be used in the Supreme Court and High Courts, and for authoritative texts of Bills and Acts.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 121 (Option 2): Restricts discussion in Parliament about the conduct of judges of the Supreme Court/High Courts, except during removal proceedings.

 

• Article 122 (Option 3): States that courts cannot inquire into Parliament's proceedings on grounds of alleged procedural irregularity.

 

• Article 119 (Option 4): Allows Parliament to regulate its own procedure relating to financial business, subject to constitutional provisions.

question: In 1526, the battle of Panipat was fought between ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Babur and Ibrahim Lodi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The First Battle of Panipat was fought on 21 April 1526 between Babur, ruler of Kabul, and Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate's Lodi dynasty. (पानीपत का प्रथम युद्ध — बाबर और इब्राहिम लोदी)

 

• Babur's victory, despite being significantly outnumbered, was largely due to effective use of field artillery and cavalry tactics such as the Tulughma (flanking manoeuvre).

 

• Ibrahim Lodi was killed in the battle, marking the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the founding of the Mughal Empire in India by Babur.

 

• The battle is considered a turning point for introducing large-scale gunpowder-based warfare in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar's forces (led by Bairam Khan) and Hemu.

 

• The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali's Afghan forces.

 

NOTE

 

• Babur and Rana Sanga (Option 1): They fought the Battle of Khanwa (1527), not the Battle of Panipat.

 

• Akbar and Hemu (Option 2): They fought the Second Battle of Panipat (1556).

 

• Humayun and Sher Khan (Option 3): Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah Suri at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540), not at Panipat.

question: Highest sex ratio according to census 2011 is of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Kerala has the highest sex ratio among Indian states, at 1,084 females per 1,000 males. (सर्वाधिक लिंगानुपात — केरल, जनगणना 2011)

 

• Kerala has consistently topped the sex ratio charts in India due to high literacy, better healthcare access, and social awareness.

 

• Among Union Territories, Puducherry has a favourable sex ratio (1,038), but among states, Kerala ranks highest.

 

• The national average sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males, an improvement over 933 in Census 2001.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among states as per Census 2011 (879 females per 1,000 males).

 

• Census 2011 was the 15th Indian census and the 7th since independence.

 

NOTE

 

• Chhattisgarh (Option 1): Has a relatively high sex ratio (991) but lower than Kerala's.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Recorded a sex ratio of 993 as per Census 2011.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Recorded a sex ratio of 996 as per Census 2011.

question: The age range for the Youth Boxer category is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17 – 18 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the age-category classification followed in amateur boxing in India (Boxing Federation of India), the Youth category covers boxers aged 17-18 years. (युवा मुक्केबाज श्रेणी — 17-18 वर्ष)

 

• Boxing competitions are organised into distinct age-based categories (such as Sub-Youth, Youth and Elite/Senior) so that boxers compete against opponents of similar age and physical development.

 

• This age-based categorisation ensures fair competition, athlete safety, and skill-appropriate matchups in the sport.

 

• Such structured age categories also form the pathway through which young boxers progress towards senior/elite level competition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) is the national governing body for amateur boxing in India.

 

• India has produced strong results in youth boxing, including medals at the Asian and World Youth/Junior Boxing Championships.

 

NOTE

 

• 15 – 16 years (Option 1): Corresponds to a younger age category, not the Youth category.

 

• 19 – 20 years (Option 2): Falls within the Elite/Senior boxer category rather than Youth.

 

• 13 – 18 years (Option 4): This range is too broad and does not correspond to the specific Youth category.

question: Hot, dry winds blowing in the Northern plain in India are known as _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The hot, dry, dust-laden winds that blow during the day across the northern and northwestern plains of India in summer (April-June) are known as "Loo". (लू — गर्म शुष्क पवनें)

 

• Loo winds typically blow from the west/northwest, are strongest in the afternoon, and can cause heatstroke; exposure to them is considered dangerous to health.

 

• They are a characteristic feature of the hot weather season in the Indo-Gangetic plains, especially in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan.

 

• Loo winds occur due to intense heating of the land surface, causing hot air to rise and sweep across the plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's hot weather season (broadly March-June) is marked by rising temperatures, loo winds, and occasional dust storms/thunderstorms called "Kal Baisakhi" in eastern India.

 

• The onset of the southwest monsoon in June brings relief from the loo by lowering temperatures and bringing rainfall.

 

NOTE

 

• North easterly winds (Option 1): Associated with the winter/retreating monsoon season, generally dry, blowing from land to sea.

 

• Westerlies (Option 2): Global prevailing winds of the mid-latitudes (roughly 30°-60°), not specific to the Indian northern plains' summer.

 

• Nor westers (Option 4): Pre-monsoon evening thunderstorms (also called "Kal Baisakhi") of West Bengal, Odisha, Assam and eastern India, distinct from the loo.

question: In which of the following Indian states is Lokrang festival observed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lokrang Festival is a folk cultural festival observed in Madhya Pradesh, typically held in Bhopal, showcasing the state's folk and tribal dance, music and art forms. (लोकरंग महोत्सव — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• It is organised by the state's Culture Department/Ustad Alauddin Khan Sangeet Evam Kala Academy, celebrating the diverse folk heritage of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• The festival features performances by folk artists and troupes from across Madhya Pradesh, promoting folk art forms and grassroots artists.

 

• It highlights the state's rich tribal and folk culture, including dance forms like Gaur, Karma and Saila.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh is also known for other cultural festivals such as the Khajuraho Dance Festival and Tansen Sangeet Samaroh.

 

• Madhya Pradesh is often referred to as the "heart of India" because of its central geographic location.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Known for festivals like Sarhul and Karma, not Lokrang.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Navratri and the Rann Utsav, not Lokrang.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Known for the Pushkar Fair and Desert Festival, not Lokrang.

question: In which among the following period Catal Huyuk was one of the most famous sites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neolithic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Çatalhöyük (Catal Huyuk), located in present-day Turkey (Anatolia), was one of the most famous and best-preserved Neolithic settlement sites, dating to roughly 7500-5700 BCE. (कैटलहुयुक — नवपाषाण युग)

 

• It is notable for its densely packed mudbrick houses accessed via rooftop entrances, evidence of early agriculture and animal domestication, and elaborate wall paintings/murals.

 

• It provides key archaeological evidence for the transition from hunting-gathering to settled agricultural life during the Neolithic Revolution.

 

• The site was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012, recognised for its significance in understanding early urban development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Neolithic period (New Stone Age) is characterised by the development of agriculture, domestication of animals, polished stone tools, and permanent settlements.

 

• Neolithic sites in India include Mehrgarh, Burzahom and Chirand.

 

NOTE

 

• Mesolithic (Option 2): The Middle Stone Age, marked by microliths and a transitional hunter-gatherer economy, predating the settled agricultural phase seen at Çatalhöyük.

 

• Palaeolithic (Option 3): The Old Stone Age, marked by hunting-gathering and crude stone tools, much earlier than Çatalhöyük.

 

• Chalcolithic (Option 4): The Copper Age, marked by the use of copper along with stone tools, chronologically later than the Neolithic.

question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from which ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Queen Elizabeth-I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The English East India Company was granted a Royal Charter by Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600, giving it a monopoly over English trade with the East Indies for 15 years. (ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी चार्टर — रानी एलिज़ाबेथ प्रथम, 1600)

 

• The charter was granted under the name "Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies".

 

• This charter marked the formal beginning of English trading activity in Asia, eventually leading to the Company's growing political and territorial influence in India.

 

• The Company's first voyage to India followed soon after, establishing its first factory in India at Surat in 1613.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The East India Company's rule in India effectively ended after the Revolt of 1857, following which the Government of India Act, 1858 transferred control to the British Crown.

 

• Other European trading companies in India during this era included the Portuguese, Dutch, French and Danish East India Companies.

 

NOTE

 

• King George-I (Option 1): Reigned much later (1714-1727), not associated with the Company's founding charter.

 

• Queen victoria (Option 3): Became Queen in 1837 and was later proclaimed Empress of India in 1876, long after the Company's original charter.

 

• King James-I (Option 4): Reigned from 1603, after the original 1600 charter was granted by Elizabeth I, though he did later renew Company privileges.

question: ‘Imperfect’ is an autobiography of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sanjay Manjrekar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Imperfect: A Life" is an autobiography written by former Indian cricketer and commentator Sanjay Manjrekar, published by HarperCollins India. (इम्परफेक्ट — संजय मांजरेकर की आत्मकथा)

 

• The book candidly discusses Manjrekar's career, personal struggles, his relationship with his father — the legendary Vijay Manjrekar — and his transition from playing to commentary.

 

• Sanjay Manjrekar represented India in Test and ODI cricket during the late 1980s and 1990s, and is now a well-known cricket commentator and analyst.

 

• The book was noted for its candour, including self-critical reflections on his cricketing career and personal life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian cricketer autobiographies include "Playing It My Way" by Sachin Tendulkar and "281 and Beyond" by V.V.S. Laxman.

 

• Sanjay Manjrekar's father, Vijay Manjrekar, was also an accomplished Indian Test cricketer.

 

NOTE

 

• Rahul Dravid (Option 1): Has not published a similarly titled autobiography.

 

• Ravi Shastri (Option 2): Former Indian cricketer and coach; "Imperfect" is not his autobiography.

 

• Milkha Singh (Option 3): His authorised biography is titled "The Race of My Life", not "Imperfect".

question:
Which of the followings HYV seeds is/are associated with the Green Revolution in India?

(A) Rice

(B) Wheat
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both Rice and Wheat High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds were central to the Green Revolution in India, which began in the mid-1960s. (हरित क्रांति — उन्नत बीज: चावल और गेहूं)

 

• The Green Revolution was pioneered with HYV wheat seeds (developed by Norman Borlaug, adapted for India by M.S. Swaminathan) and later extended to HYV rice varieties (including IR8, developed at IRRI).

 

• These HYV seeds, combined with irrigation, fertilizers and pesticides, significantly boosted foodgrain production, particularly in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

• M.S. Swaminathan is widely regarded as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for introducing and adapting HYV wheat and rice seeds to Indian conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution significantly increased India's wheat and rice production, helping the country move towards self-sufficiency in foodgrains.

 

• Criticisms of the Green Revolution include regional disparities, over-dependence on chemical fertilizers/pesticides, and depletion of groundwater resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Only A (Option 2): Incorrect, as it omits Wheat, which was equally central to the Green Revolution.

 

• Neither A nor B (Option 3): Incorrect, since both crops were key beneficiaries of HYV seed technology.

 

• Only B (Option 4): Incorrect, as it omits Rice, which was also a major beneficiary of HYV seeds.

question: In Tennis which of the following scores is a complete set?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6-4.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In tennis, a player must win at least 6 games with a margin of at least 2 games to win a set outright; a score of 6-4 satisfies this and represents a complete, valid set. (टेनिस सेट स्कोर — 6-4)

 

• At 6-5, the set is not yet complete — the leading player must win one more game (to reach 7-5) or the trailing player must level it to 6-6.

 

• At 6-6, most tournaments use a tie-break game to decide the set (making it 7-6), so 6-6 by itself is not a complete set score.

 

• A score like 5-3 is also incomplete, since neither player has reached the minimum of 6 games required to win a set.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A tennis match is typically played as best-of-three or best-of-five sets, depending on the tournament and gender category.

 

• The tie-break system was introduced to prevent excessively long sets when players kept winning alternate games.

 

NOTE

 

• 5-3 (Option 1): Incomplete — neither player has reached 6 games yet.

 

• 6-6 (Option 3): Requires a tie-break to be decided (usually becoming 7-6); not itself a final/complete set score.

 

• 6-5 (Option 4): Incomplete — play continues until one player leads by 2 games or a tie-break is triggered at 6-6.

question: Identify a protein-digesting enzyme.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pepsin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pepsin is a protein-digesting (proteolytic) enzyme secreted by the gastric glands of the stomach in its inactive form pepsinogen, activated by hydrochloric acid (HCl). (पेप्सिन — प्रोटीन पाचक एंजाइम)

 

• Pepsin breaks down proteins into smaller peptides by cleaving peptide bonds, working optimally in the stomach's highly acidic environment (pH around 1.5-2).

 

• It plays a key role in the initial stage of protein digestion, before further breakdown occurs in the small intestine by enzymes like trypsin and chymotrypsin.

 

• Pepsin was one of the first enzymes discovered, identified by Theodor Schwann in 1836.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other digestive enzymes include amylase (digests starch/carbohydrates), lipase (digests fats), and trypsin (digests proteins in the small intestine).

 

• The stomach's acidic environment, maintained by HCl from parietal cells, also helps kill many ingested pathogens.

 

NOTE

 

• lipase (Option 1): Digests fats (lipids) into fatty acids and glycerol, not proteins.

 

• Amylase (Option 2): Digests carbohydrates (starch) into simpler sugars, not proteins.

 

• Collagen (Option 3): A structural protein found in connective tissue, skin and bones — it is not an enzyme.

question: Which of the following became India’s first State Assembly to implement the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) programme to become paperless?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nagaland became India's first State Legislative Assembly to fully implement the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) programme, making it a completely paperless assembly. (नागालैंड — पहली पेपरलेस विधानसभा, नेवा)

 

• NeVA is a Mission Mode Project under the Digital India programme, developed to digitise and integrate the legislative processes of state assemblies/legislative councils onto a single unified platform.

 

• The Nagaland Legislative Assembly achieved this fully paperless status around March 2022, integrating digital bill tracking, questions, and other legislative business.

 

• NeVA aims to connect all Vidhan Sabhas across states to a central server and provide citizens a common platform to access legislative information.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NeVA is implemented under the aegis of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Government of India.

 

• Several other states have since progressively adopted e-Vidhan/NeVA to digitise legislative processes, following Nagaland's lead as the first fully paperless assembly.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 1): Was not the first state to achieve this distinction under NeVA.

 

• Tripura (Option 2): Was not the first state to achieve this distinction under NeVA.

 

• Assam (Option 4): Was not the first state to achieve this distinction under NeVA.

question: Who among the following ruler ruled before Prithviraj Chauhan over Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ananga Pala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ananga Pala (Anangpal Tomar), a ruler of the Tomar dynasty of Delhi, ruled over Delhi before Prithviraj Chauhan, who was his grandson (through his daughter). (अनंगपाल तोमर — पृथ्वीराज चौहान से पूर्व दिल्ली के शासक)

 

• Since Anangpal Tomar had no son, he made his grandson Prithviraj Chauhan (son of Someshwar Chauhan and Anangpal's daughter) his heir, who succeeded to the throne of Delhi.

 

• The Tomars were an important Rajput dynasty who founded and ruled Delhi (then called Dhillika/Dhilli) before the Chauhans (Chahamanas) took over.

 

• Anangpal Tomar is also credited with founding the city of Delhi (Lal Kot) and with structures near the present-day Qutub complex.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan (Prithviraj III) was defeated by Muhammad of Ghor at the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), a turning point leading to the establishment of Muslim rule in Delhi.

 

• The Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty was based primarily in Ajmer before extending control to Delhi through Prithviraj III's succession.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (Option 1): A later Delhi Sultanate ruler of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty (r. 1266-1287), succeeding well after Prithviraj Chauhan's reign.

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji (Option 3): Founder of the Khalji dynasty, ruling Delhi from 1290, well after Prithviraj Chauhan.

 

• Qutbuddin Aybak (Option 4): Founder of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1206, after defeating Prithviraj Chauhan's successors — i.e., after, not before, Prithviraj Chauhan's era.

question: Motion of an object is ______ if its velocity is constant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is uniform.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Motion of an object is termed "uniform motion" when it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, which corresponds to the object having a constant velocity. (एकसमान गति — स्थिर वेग)

 

• Since velocity is a vector quantity involving both speed and direction, a constant velocity means the object moves in a straight line at a constant speed, without acceleration.

 

• In uniform motion, the acceleration is zero, because there is no change in velocity over time.

 

• Uniform motion is contrasted with non-uniform motion, in which velocity changes over time (in magnitude, direction, or both), such as during acceleration or deceleration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The equation of uniform motion is distance = speed × time, with speed remaining constant throughout.

 

• A vehicle moving at a constant, unchanging speed along a straight road is a common real-world approximation of uniform motion.

 

NOTE

 

• only accelerating (Option 1): Acceleration implies increasing velocity over time, contradicting a constant velocity.

 

• only decelerating (Option 2): Deceleration implies decreasing velocity over time, also contradicting a constant velocity.

 

• non-uniform (Option 3): Non-uniform motion involves changing velocity (unequal distances in equal time intervals) — the opposite of the constant-velocity scenario described.
